newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu returns to France amidst health worries.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu returns to France amidst health worries.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko arrived in southern France on Thursday, leaving his African nation in the throes of a rebel uprising.

Mobutu's private aircraft landed in the Riviera capital Nice at around 1.15 p.m. (1215 GMT), airport officials said. In Paris, the French Foreign Ministry said the Zairean head of state had a three-month visa.

Mobutu's spokesman said the president, who has spent only three weeks in Zaire since last August, was in France to consult his doctors following treatment for prostate cancer in Switzerland last year.
But rebel leader Laurent Kabila said the head of state was simply fleeing Zaire.

"Those soldiers who still supported Mobutu expected that his presence would turn the tide against us, and now they can see he is fleeing the country they will be even more demoralised," Kabila told Reuters.
"While he goes off to France all Mobutu has left with his people are foreign mercenaries."
Before returning to Zaire three weeks ago, Mobutu had spent six weeks at his palatial villa in the Riviera town of Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, where aides said he was recuperating from cancer treatment.

On his return to Zaire, he had carried out a major reshuffle in the government and the army high command in preparation for an intended counter-attack on positions captured by rebels holding a large tract of eastern Zaire.
The rebels have vowed to march to Kinshasa to overthrow the president, who has ruled the mineral-rich country for 31 years.

Mobutu flew to France from his jungle palace at Gbadolite, where he stayed for much of the time after returning on December 17 to a huge welcome by well over 100,000 inhabitants of the capital, Kinshasa.

It was a brief hour of glory. Soon afterwards, he was drawing renewed attacks from political enemies over his decision to retain much-criticised Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo at the head of a new crisis government formed on Christmas Eve.
The rebels have advanced from the North and South Kivu area they originally controlled and fighting has raged around the eastern town of Bunia in Upper Zaire.
The alliance that began the rebellion with a group of mostly ethnic Tutsis now occupies a 500-km (300-mile) swathe of eastern Zaire along the border with Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda.
Mobutu has ruled out negotiation with rebel leader Kabila and vowed to crush him. But analysts say the Zairean government is not in a position to inflict heavy losses on the better-equipped rebels.

A much-trumpeted counter-attack against the ethnic Tutsi rebels, who Zaire says are backed by Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi, has so far failed to materialise with Zaire's retreating army plagued by problems of discipline.
On Wednesday the rebels called on France, Belgium, South Africa and others to stop their citizens joining a mercenary force they say is supporting the army.

"We want to dissuade these countries from allowing their people to serve a criminal and prolong his stay in power," the rebels' foreign affairs spokesman Kakudji Gaetan told a news conference in Goma.
Kakudji said mercenaries from France, Belgium, South Africa, Angola and Togo were being assembled by Mobutu along with soldiers of the former Rwandan army in exile in Zaire.
